results.prompt: Tanong lang: ano ang pagkakaiba ng Notes at plain-text editor? Huwag kang gumalaw ng app para dito.
results.transcript:
🤖 KURT

**Notes vs. plain‑text editor (TextEdit) sa macOS**

| Aspeto | **Notes** | **Plain‑text editor (TextEdit) – “plain‑text mode”** |
|--------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary purpose** | Quick memos, checklists, voice notes, sketches, at 
pag‑sync sa iCloud para ma‑access sa iPhone, iPad, at Mac. | Simple word 
processor para magsulat ng puro text (walang rich‑formatting) o RTF kung gusto 
mo. |
| **File type / storage** | Mga nota ay naka‑store bilang bahagi ng Notes app 
database (walang .txt o .rtf file na makikita mo directly). | Maaari kang 
mag‑save ng .txt (plain) o .rtf files na makikita at mabuksan ng iba pang 
editor. |
| **Formatting** | Limited – bullet points, headings, tables, images, drawings, 
attachments, pero hindi full‑blown formatting gaya ng fonts/size (hindi tulad ng
Word). | Sa plain‑text mode, **walang** formatting (walang bold, italics, 
fonts). Sa RTF mode, meron kang basic formatting. |
| **Sync / iCloud** | Auto‑sync sa iCloud across devices; kung naka‑on ang 
iCloud Notes, makikita mo agad ang notes sa lahat ng Apple device. | Sync only 
kung manu‑man mong i‑save ang file sa iCloud Drive or another cloud folder. |
| **Search & organization** | May folders, tags (sa newer macOS), at mabilis na 
search sa loob ng app. | Search ay depende sa Finder (or Spotlight) at folder 
organization mo. |
| **Integration** | Madaling i‑share to Messages, Mail, Safari “Add to Notes,” 
at “Copy Link to Note.” | Export / import as plain text; walang built‑in sharing
shortcuts like Notes. |
| **Quick capture** | pwede mong buksan gamit ang **Control‑Space → “Notes”** o 
gamit ang **Command‑N** sa widget; even Siri can create a note. | Kailangan mong
buksan TextEdit o gumamit ng Spotlight (⌘‑Space → “TextEdit”) para magsimula. |
| **Multimedia** | Support sa images, sketches, checklists, mga attachment, at 
voice recordings. | Plain‑text mode: **walang** media support; RTF mode may 
embed images pero hindi as seamlessly as Notes. |
| **Versioning / Undo** | May simple undo, pero walang built‑in version history.
| TextEdit also has undo; kung i‑save as file, macOS may file‑level versioning 
(via Time Machine/Versions). |

**Bottom line:**  
- **Notes** ay para sa mabilis, synced, multimedia‑friendly na pag‑tala na 
accessible sa lahat ng Apple device.  
- **Plain‑text editor** (TextEdit in plain‑text mode) ay para sa simpleng, 
walang‑format na text files na madaling i‑share, i‑store, at i‑edit sa kahit 
anong editor o command‑line tool.  

Kung gusto mo lang mag‑type ng simpleng dokumento at balak i‑save later as .txt,
TextEdit ang gamitin. Kung gusto mo ng mabilis na note na awtomatikong sync at 
may support sa images o checklists, go with **Notes**.
